study_description: You will watch 8 pairs of sports videos (student vs. expert) and rate three coaching feedback variants on four dimensions. Variants are labelled A / B / C and presented in randomised order. Please do not discuss your ratings with other participants.

metrics.name: Corrective Utility
metrics.description: Does the feedback give a specific, actionable physical correction (not generic advice)?

metrics.name: Expert Alignment
metrics.description: Does the feedback support the core intent of what an expert would say? (A specific biomechanically-sound tip should not be penalised even if the ground-truth is vague.)

metrics.name: Hallucination Check
metrics.description: Does the feedback contradict observable evidence or suggest physically impossible movements? (5 = no contradiction; 1 = significant biomechanical error.)

metrics.name: Information Density
metrics.description: Does the feedback contain high-value technical insight vs. filler? (1 = high fluff; 5 = dense with professional insights.)

preference_question: Overall, which single feedback would you most recommend to the student?

samples.gt: The player's release point and direction do not qualify as a reverse layup.

feedbacks.text: Keep your elbows tucked and maintain a stable center of mass to enhance your shooting form.
Focus on improving your overall body coordination to perform better in basketball drills.
Drive your lead knee higher during the approach and release the ball at the peak of your jump, extending your wrist fully for a proper reverse layup finish.

samples.gt: The student's hip rotation is insufficient and the plant foot is too far from the ball.

feedbacks.text: Try to kick the ball with more power and aim more accurately.
Plant your non-kicking foot closer to the ball and rotate your hips fully through contact to generate more power.
Increase your hip rotation during the kick to improve the force transmission from your trunk to your foot.

samples.gt: The climber needs to improve their route-reading skills by glancing ahead to plan their next moves.

feedbacks.text: Keep your hips closer to the wall and push through your legs rather than pulling with your arms to conserve upper-body strength.
Before each move, look two holds ahead to plan your body position and reduce unnecessary arm fatigue.
Try to climb more efficiently by planning your movements in advance.

samples.gt: The student lacks a consistent alternating footwork pattern and releases too early.

feedbacks.text: Work on your timing and footwork to make your Mikan layup more consistent.
Focus on alternating your take-off foot on each side of the basket and delay your release until your elbow is above the rim.
Increase your knee drive on each step and release the ball at the top of your jump arc to establish a rhythmic left-right pattern.

samples.gt: The student's touch is too heavy and body posture is too upright, reducing close control.

feedbacks.text: Use lighter, more frequent touches and lean slightly forward over the ball to improve your close control at speed.
Keep the ball closer to your body and use smaller touches to maintain better control.
Improve your dribbling technique by keeping the ball under control at all times.

samples.gt: The student's elbow flares out and the follow-through is incomplete.

feedbacks.text: Snap your wrist fully at release and hold the follow-through position — elbow aligned with the basket — until the ball hits the rim.
Keep your elbow directly under the ball and extend your shooting arm fully on release to straighten your shot trajectory.
Focus on your shooting form and try to be more consistent with your release.

samples.gt: The student over-grips and fails to use footholds effectively, causing early muscle fatigue.

feedbacks.text: Trust your feet more — shift your weight onto your footholds and relax your grip on the holds to reduce forearm fatigue.
Try to use your legs more and rely less on your arms when climbing.
Engage your lower body more actively by pressing through your feet on each move, which will reduce the load on your fingers and forearms.

samples.gt: The student approaches from the wrong angle and uses the wrong hand for the reverse finish.

feedbacks.text: Approach the basket from the opposite side and use your far hand to lay the ball up off the backboard with a soft touch.
Work on using the correct hand and approach angle for the reverse layup.
On a reverse layup, attack the baseline, keep your body between the defender and the ball, and release with your outside hand at the peak of your jump.
